heat_classical: Prediction matches the reference diffusion field almost exactly; the t=0.25/0.50/0.75 snapshots show the red model dashes sitting on top of the black reference with no visible amplitude cap (peaks ~0.8, 0.6, 0.47 all reproduced). |error| stays under ~0.021 and is concentrated in thin bands at the top and bottom edges near x=+/-0.75 to +/-1.0 (worst spot lower-left near t=0, x=-0.8). The Fourier spectrum tracks the reference bar-for-bar all the way to k=20 with only tiny per-harmonic deviations, and the only mismatch is k=0 where the model shows a small ~0.1 offset vs the reference near-zero mean. Inference: a smooth low-frequency heat solution is fit essentially perfectly by the classical PINN with no spectral-bias cutoff.
heat_qapinn: Quantum model reproduces the smooth heat field well; snapshot dashes overlie the reference with only a hair of amplitude softening (prediction colorbar tops ~0.86 vs reference 1.0 at the t=0 initial peak). |error| peaks ~0.013 (lower than the classical run's 0.02) and forms swirled patches on the left edge near t=0, strongest around x=-0.85. Spectrum matches the reference through k=20 with a spurious k=0 bar (~0.1) as the only real defect. Entanglement S(x,t) is smooth, ranging ~0.35 (dark trough near x=0.1, t=0.1) to ~1.2 (bright upper-right, x>0.5 and t>0.5), and the four <Z> qubit maps are clean low-frequency receptive fields (qubit 0 a strong horizontal x-band). Inference: on an easy smooth problem the QAPINN matches or slightly beats the classical PINN while using low, spatially-structured entanglement.
burgers_classical: The model completely fails to capture the Burgers shock at x=0: the prediction is a smooth sawtooth with amplitude capped at ~0.7 (colorbar max ~0.68) versus the reference's sharp +/-1.0 jump. Snapshots show the red model rounding off the steep gradient and undershooting both lobes (e.g. t=0.5 model peak ~0.6 vs reference ~1.0), and |error| forms a bright bowtie straddling x=0 that reaches ~0.9. The spectrum matches only k=1-2, then the model falls progressively below the reference from k~3 onward, ending roughly 1.5-2 decades low by k=20 (model ~1e-2 vs reference ~1). Inference: classic spectral bias, the smooth network cannot represent the high-harmonic content of the discontinuity.
burgers_qapinn: Behaves almost identically to the classical Burgers run: shock at x=0 is smeared into a rounded sawtooth with amplitude capped at ~0.65 (colorbar ~0.66), and |error| shows the same bright bowtie about x=0 peaking ~0.9. Spectrum agrees at k=1-2 then drops below the reference from k~3, reaching about 1.5 decades low at k=20 (model ~0.04 vs ~1). Entanglement S ranges ~0.45 (dark band near x=0-0.25) to ~1.05 (bright bottom-left corner x<-0.5,t<0.2), and qubit 0 again carries a dominant horizontal band while qubits 1-3 show milder diagonal structure. Inference: quantum embedding does not overcome the shock/spectral-bias limitation, matching the classical PINN's failure mode almost exactly.
abl_baseline: Identical to burgers_qapinn (same figures): smeared shock, amplitude capped ~0.65, |error| bowtie about x=0 peaking ~0.9. Spectrum matches k=1-2 then falls below the reference from k~3, ~1.5 decades low by k=20. Entanglement S spans ~0.45 to ~1.05 with the bright corner at bottom-left (x<-0.5, t<0.2) and a dark band near x=0; qubit 0 shows the strong horizontal x-band. Inference: this is the reference depth configuration and it sits at the moderate-entanglement, shock-limited operating point that the depth ablations vary around.
abl_depth_1: Shallowest circuit and the weakest fit: prediction amplitude is capped hardest at ~0.6 (colorbar ~0.6) and the sawtooth is the most rounded of the set, with the |error| bowtie about x=0 still reaching ~0.9. Spectrum tracks k=1-2 then drops below reference from k~2-3 with the model bars flattening to ~0.06-0.08 by k=20. Most notably the entanglement collapses to a low range S ~0.05-0.55 (far below baseline's ~1.05), concentrated only in the upper-right corner (x>0.5, t>0.8); the <Z> maps are simple monotone gradients with little structure. Inference: too few layers starves the model of entanglement/expressivity, giving the lowest amplitude and flattest high-k response.
abl_depth_2: Intermediate depth: prediction still amplitude-capped ~0.6 with the same smeared shock and ~0.9 |error| bowtie about x=0, so solution quality is barely changed from depth 1. Spectrum matches k=1-2 then falls below reference from k~3, similar to baseline. Entanglement recovers to a mid range S ~0.35-0.98 (bright peak in the top-right corner, dark patch bottom-right), sitting between depth_1 (~0.55 max) and baseline (~1.05 max); qubits 0-1 show antisymmetric horizontal bands while qubits 2-3 are fainter. Inference: added depth mainly raises entanglement capacity but yields only marginal gains in the realized shock solution.
abl_depth_5: Deepest circuit and marginally the best of the Burgers/ablation set: prediction amplitude recovers to ~0.65 and the sawtooth is slightly sharper, though the shock is still smoothed and the |error| bowtie about x=0 remains ~0.9. Spectrum holds a hair closer to the reference through mid-k but still falls off from k~3, ending ~0.05 at k=20. Entanglement is the highest and most structured, S ~0.6-1.2, with a distinct bright blob at x~0,t~0.3 (~1.2) and a dark trough near x=-0.5,t~0.7 (~0.6); the <Z> qubit maps are visibly more oscillatory with sign changes across qubits. Inference: more layers monotonically increase entanglement (0.55 -> 0.98 -> 1.05 -> 1.2 across depths 1/2/baseline/5) and richer qubit features, but only modestly improve the shock fit, confirming depth helps expressivity more than it cures spectral bias.
abl_ent_none: Prediction amplitude caps at ~+/-0.6 vs the reference +/-1.0, so the model reproduces the smooth sinusoidal ramps but rounds off both peaks; the |error| map (peaking ~0.9) concentrates in a bright horizontal band at the x=0 shock, widening toward t~0.4-0.6, and the t=0.25/0.50/0.75 slices show the red model curve completely failing to capture the steepening jump at x=0. The realized Fourier spectrum tracks the reference for k=1-2 but the model bars fall progressively below reference from about k=4 onward and drop roughly an order of magnitude by k~11-12. Entanglement entropy is essentially zero (colorbar scale 1e-7, values within +/-6e-7, just numerical noise in a faint checkerboard), confirming the product-state/no-entangler wiring; per-qubit <Z> maps show clean, well-differentiated structure (qubits 0 and 2 horizontal x-banded, qubits 1 and 3 vertical t-gradients). Inference: with entanglement disabled the circuit still fits low harmonics via the classical net but cannot represent the shock, so this run behaves like a purely classical PINN with the QC layer contributing nothing.
abl_ent_ring: Prediction again caps near +/-0.6 with the same shock-band error structure (|error| ~0.9 along x=0), and the slice plots show the smooth model curve missing the sharp jump identically to the none run. Spectrum matches reference at k=1-2 then rolls off, model bars sitting ~1 order below reference by k~10. Critically the entanglement entropy is now substantial and non-trivial, ranging roughly 0.62-1.25 von Neumann units with a smooth spatial pattern (high entropy ~1.2 in the upper-left x>0.5/t<0.3 region, a dark low-entropy pocket ~0.65 near x~-0.5/t~0). The loss landscape shows a well-defined minimum but with a secondary basin toward the lower-left, and F-principle 'iter to halve' sits at ~250. Inference: ring entanglement switches the circuit into a genuinely entangled regime (S~1), yet the shock fit is essentially unchanged from none, suggesting the entangler adds correlation without improving expressivity for this discontinuity.
abl_ent_all_to_all: Prediction caps ~+/-0.65 with the familiar x=0 shock error band (~0.9), and slices show the same rounded-peak, no-jump behavior. Spectrum tracks reference to k~2 then the model falls below, ~1 order down by k~10. Entanglement entropy is moderate, ~0.45-1.05, with a distinctive smooth structure: a low-entropy dip (~0.45) centered at x~0.1/t~0.5 and higher entropy (~1.0) at the corners/edges (bottom-right t~1). Notably the extrapolation curve is the worst of the entanglement set, rising past relative-L2 = 1.0 by t=1.5 (vs ~0.5-0.6 for none/ring), and F-principle iter-to-halve is highest at ~575. Inference: full all-to-all connectivity produces the strongest entanglement gradients but the poorest temporal extrapolation and slowest frequency convergence, indicating the denser entangler over-parameterizes/harms generalization without fixing the in-domain shock.
abl_post_lin: With no hidden post-net ([]), the prediction cap drops to the lowest ~+/-0.55 and the error band at x=0 is correspondingly the most pronounced; slices show the flattest, most under-amplitude model curves of the post series. Spectrum matches k=1-2 then rolls off ~1 order by k~10, similar shape to baseline. Entanglement entropy ranges ~0.6-1.15 with a yellow high-entropy blob at x~0.4/t~0.9 and a dark low pocket ~0.6 at x~-0.3/t~0. The F-principle right panel is EMPTY (no data point plotted, axes autoscaled to +/-0.05), and the per-frequency heatmap shows only k=0-2 with slow red convergence. Inference: removing the classical post-net (linear readout only) yields the weakest amplitude fit, confirming the post-net is what lets the model push output amplitude toward the reference; the missing F-principle marker suggests the halving metric failed/never triggered here.
abl_post_8: Prediction cap recovers to ~+/-0.63 (higher than post_lin), and the slice fits are visibly the best-amplitude of the series, with the model curve reaching ~0.63 at t=0.25; error still bands at the x=0 shock (~0.9) but in-domain smooth regions fit tightly. Spectrum matches reference through k~2 then declines ~1 order by k~10. Entanglement entropy ~0.55-1.0 with a bright high-entropy lobe (~1.0) in the lower-left x<-0.25/t<0.4 and a dark low corner (~0.55) upper-left. This run shows the best generalization: extrapolation relative-L2 bottoms ~0.42 right at the train|extrapolate boundary and only rises to ~0.55 by t=1.5; neurons.png correctly shows 8 receptive fields. The F-principle right panel is again EMPTY. Inference: an 8-wide post-net already restores near-full amplitude and gives the tightest extrapolation, implying the post-net width delivers most of its benefit by width 8.
abl_post_32: Prediction cap ~+/-0.63, comparable to post_8 and the baseline, with the same x=0 shock error band (~0.9) and rounded-peak slices. Spectrum tracks reference to k~2 then rolls off ~1 order by k~10, essentially unchanged from the narrower nets. Entanglement entropy ~0.45-1.0 with high-entropy ridge (~0.95-1.0) across x~0-0.25 spanning t, and a dark low-entropy pocket (~0.45) at x~-0.5/t~0.8. Extrapolation dips to ~0.36 near t=1.1 then climbs to ~0.55 by t=1.5, similar to post_8; loss landscape has a clean central minimum with a mild secondary lower basin, and F-principle iter-to-halve ~375 (fastest of the runs that reported it). Neurons panel shows 12 fields but several (5,7,9,10,11) are very washed-out/low-contrast. Inference: widening the post-net to 32 does not improve amplitude or shock fit beyond width 8 and leaves many neurons near-inactive, indicating the extra width is largely redundant for this problem.
abl_qubits_3: Prediction colorbar spans about +/-0.6 versus the reference +/-1.0, and the t=0.25/0.50/0.75 snapshots show the red model curve peaking near 0.58 while the black reference reaches 1.0, so the model captures the sinusoidal shape but strongly under-shoots the sawtooth amplitude. The |error| map (colorbar to ~0.9) is concentrated in a bright fan around the shock at x=0 that widens with t, and the qubits panel shows exactly 3 <Z_i> maps; entanglement entropy is low, ranging only ~0.1 to 0.65 with a dark low-entropy band near x=-0.25. The loss landscape is a clean single convex basin (min log10 loss ~ -0.9 at the red star). Inference: with only 3 qubits the circuit lacks the expressivity/frequency support to resolve the steep shock, so it settles into a smooth amplitude-limited approximation.
abl_qubits_5: Prediction reaches about +/-0.65 and the snapshot model curves peak near 0.60 (still short of the reference 1.0), a modest improvement over the 3-qubit run. The qubits panel now shows 5 <Z_i> maps (one full row of 4 plus qubit 4), the error fan at x=0 tops out near 0.9, and entanglement entropy rises to a higher range of ~0.55 to 1.1 with a low-entropy pocket near (t=0.3, x=-0.3). The generalization curve dips to its minimum (~0.42 relative L2) just past the train|extrapolate line at t~1.1 before rising to ~0.65 by t=1.5. Inference: adding qubits increases available entanglement and slightly improves amplitude recovery, confirming a mild capacity benefit without fully resolving the shock.
abl_qubits_6: Prediction spans roughly +/-0.6 to 0.65 with snapshot peaks near 0.6, comparable to the 5-qubit case, and the |error| colorbar now reaches the full 1.0 in the shock fan at x=0. The qubits panel displays 6 <Z_i> maps (4+2), and entanglement entropy is the highest of the qubit sweep, ranging ~0.65 up to ~1.35 with a dark low-entropy blob near (t=0.15, x=0.2). The Fourier spectrum tracks the reference through k~3 then the model bars fall increasingly below reference for k>4. Inference: entanglement scales monotonically with qubit count (3->~0.65, 5->~1.1, 6->~1.35) yet reconstruction accuracy saturates, indicating diminishing returns beyond ~5 qubits for this Burgers problem.
abl_meas_single: Single-Z readout gives the weakest amplitude of the measurement variants: the prediction colorbar is only +/-0.5 and snapshot model peaks reach ~0.47 versus reference 1.0. The error fan around x=0 brightens to ~0.9, the qubits panel shows 4 <Z_i> maps, and entanglement entropy runs ~0.68 to 1.05 with a bright high-entropy band in the upper half (x>0.5) and dark pockets at the corners. The realized spectrum matches reference at k=1 but model harmonics for k>=4 sit ~1 order below reference. Inference: restricting the observable to a single-qubit Z expectation limits the expressible output range, producing the smallest-amplitude fit and confirming the readout choice caps reconstruction fidelity.
abl_meas_zz: ZZ-correlator readout restores amplitude close to the multi-qubit baseline: prediction spans +/-0.65 and snapshot model peaks reach ~0.58, clearly better than the single-Z run. The qubits panel shows 4 <Z_i> maps, the shock error fan reaches ~0.9, and entanglement entropy ranges ~0.45 to 1.2 with a bright high-entropy corner at (t=0, x=0.9) and a dark low-entropy pocket near (t=1.0, x=-0.8). The Fourier spectrum follows the reference through the first several harmonics before the usual high-k roll-off. Inference: two-qubit ZZ observables carry substantially more expressive power than single-Z, recovering near-baseline accuracy and making readout richness more impactful than raw qubit count.
abl_scale_05: With input_scale=0.5 the encoding under-activates: prediction is only +/-0.5 and snapshot model peaks ~0.50, the lowest-amplitude smooth fit of the scale sweep. The 4 qubit <Z_i> maps are very smooth and low-contrast (mostly pale purple, little orange), and entanglement entropy is smooth and modest (~0.53 to 0.95), increasing left-to-right in t toward a bright band around x=0. The error fan at x=0 reaches ~0.9 and the spectrum shows the model decaying faster than reference beyond k~4. Inference: a small encoding scale compresses the input into a near-linear region of the feature map, limiting accessible frequencies and yielding an under-fit, over-smooth solution.
abl_scale_pi: At input_scale=pi the prediction (+/-0.5) becomes visibly noisy: the 2D map shows patchy blotches instead of the clean two-lobe structure, and snapshot model curves (~0.47 peak) carry small oscillatory wiggles rather than a smooth arc. The 4 qubit <Z_i> maps display clear mid-frequency oscillations/banding, and entanglement entropy is patchy and disordered, ranging ~0.2 to 1.1 with scattered dark and bright cells rather than smooth gradients. The error fan at x=0 reaches ~0.85. Inference: pushing the encoding scale to pi begins to over-fold the input, injecting spurious high-frequency content and marking the onset of the instability that fully collapses at 2pi.
abl_scale_2pi: Collapse confirmed: the prediction colorbar spans only about -0.015 to -0.002 (|u| ~ 0.01, effectively zero) and shows fine speckled noise, while all three snapshot model lines are flat at u ~ 0 straight across, completely missing the reference sawtooth. Because the prediction is ~0, the |error| map equals the reference amplitude with the colorbar saturating at 1.0, and the Fourier spectrum shows the model k>=1 harmonics collapsed to ~1e-2 to 1e-1, far below the reference bars. The 4 qubit <Z_i> maps are dominated by high-frequency horizontal striping (aliasing) and entanglement entropy is fully disordered noise (~0.3 to 1.1). Inference: input_scale=2pi aliases the encoding so severely that the optimizer finds only the trivial u~0 solution, a total collapse consistent with the expected failure mode.
abl_cls_29: Smallest net: the shock is entirely erased into a smooth low-amplitude sine, with the model peak capped at about +-0.55 versus the reference +-1.0, and the t=0.50 near-vertical front replaced by a gentle slope. Error is a bright plume emanating from x=0 that grows with t and biases to the +x side, peaking near |error|~0.9. Spectrum: model matches only the k=1 fundamental (~60 vs reference ~80) and every harmonic k>=2 sits well below reference, dropping ~1-2 decades low by k>=4 (also a spurious nonzero k=0 mean ~2). Inference: at this capacity the network only fits the smooth envelope and has zero shock resolution.
abl_cls_73: Almost indistinguishable from the 29-param run: amplitude capped at ~+-0.57, the shock at t=0.50 rounded to a smooth curve with no discontinuity, and error concentrated in the same x~0 plume peaking ~0.9. Spectrum tracks k=1 (~60 vs 80) but falls monotonically below reference from k=2 onward, roughly 1 decade low across k=6-20. Inference: doubling params from 29 buys no visible shock sharpening.
abl_cls_99: Noticeably better: amplitude reaches ~+-0.73 and the front becomes asymmetric/tilted (steeper just left of x=0 with an inflection at x~0) rather than a symmetric sine, so it begins to hint at the shock. Error plume peak is a bit higher (~1.05) but the low-x region is cleaner, and the spectrum keeps model bars within ~factor 3 of reference out to about k=6-7 before rolling off. Inference: this mid-count net is the first to partially resolve the shock geometry, not just the envelope.
abl_cls_105: Regresses relative to 99: amplitude back down to ~+-0.55 and the front smoothed into a symmetric sine with no tilt. Error plume from x=0 peaks ~0.9 and spreads on the +x side; spectrum matches k=1 (~50 vs 80) then falls ~1 decade below reference for k>=4. Inference: more parameters than 99 here yield a worse, purely smooth fit, so capacity alone does not help the shock.
abl_cls_113: Amplitude capped at ~+-0.62, slightly higher than 105 but still a rounded front with no true steepening at t=0.50. Error stays in the x~0 plume (peak ~0.85) biased to +x; spectrum tracks k=1 (~55 vs 80) and sits ~0.5-1 decade below reference from k>=3 out to k=20. Inference: modest amplitude gain, still no shock resolution.
abl_cls_121: One of the weaker fits: amplitude capped low at ~+-0.50 with a flat, symmetric-sine profile and no front steepening. Error plume peaks ~0.85 near x=0; spectrum matches only k=1 (~55 vs 80) and drops below reference for all k>=2, ~1 decade low by k=5. Inference: despite more params than 99, the shock is not captured at all.
abl_cls_137: Amplitude ~+-0.58 with the shock rounded into a smooth curve; the t=0.50 near-jump is missed entirely. Error is the familiar x~0 plume (peak ~0.9) skewed to +x, and the spectrum tracks k=1 (~55 vs 80) then rolls off ~1 decade below reference for k>=4. Inference: a plain smooth approximation, no capacity benefit over the small nets.
abl_cls_143: Degenerate/worst run: the prediction collapses into near-static horizontal bands that barely evolve with t, amplitude capped lowest at ~+-0.46, and no front steepening whatsoever. The |error| plume is broad and reaches to large |x| (peak ~0.9), and the spectrum is ragged with several harmonics (k~2,8,10) 1-2 decades below reference. Inference: this larger net underfits badly, direct evidence that adding parameters can hurt rather than sharpen the shock.
abl_cls_165: Best shock rendering of the set: amplitude reaches ~+-0.68 and the front is clearly tilted and steepened with a visible overshoot/kink near x~0.3-0.5, closest to the reference discontinuity. Error plume is the dimmest here (peak ~0.85) and confined tightly to x~0, while the spectrum keeps model bars within ~factor 2-3 of reference out to about k=7-8 before rolling off. Inference: a mid-large count that actually improves shock geometry, showing the benefit is non-monotonic in parameter count.
abl_cls_169: Back to a smooth, symmetric fit: amplitude capped at ~+-0.55 with no front steepening at t=0.50. Error plume peaks ~0.9 near x=0 and biases to +x; spectrum matches k=1 (~55 vs 80) and sits ~1 decade below reference for k>=4 out to k=20. Inference: more params than 165 yet a clearly worse, envelope-only fit.
abl_cls_217: Largest net but unremarkable: amplitude capped at ~+-0.57 with the shock rounded into a smooth curve, no true steepening. Error stays in the x~0 plume (peak ~0.9) skewed to +x, and the spectrum tracks k=1 (~40 vs 80) then falls ~0.5-1 decade below reference across k>=4. Inference: the highest parameter count does not produce the sharpest shock (165 and 99 are better), so capacity is not the limiting factor here.
cfe_burgers: Burgers shock at x=0: the classical-front-end model renders it as a smooth ramp, never a jump, so the peak amplitude saturates near |u|~0.7 versus the reference +/-1.0 at t=0.25. Absolute error is a bright lobe (~1.0) hugging the x=0 shock line and growing from t~0.2 outward; away from the shock the field is dark (<0.1). Spectrum matches k=1 (~70) but the model coefficients roll off steadily to ~0.05 by k>=10 while the reference stays on a ~1-5 plateau out to k=20. Inference: without real quantum layers the front-end acts as a low-pass filter that cannot synthesize the high harmonics needed for a sharp shock.
cfe_heat: Heat diffusion of a sine: reference and prediction are visually identical smooth blue/red bands, and the t=0.25/0.50/0.75 slices overlay almost perfectly (peaks ~0.79, 0.61, 0.48). |error| is tiny, ~0.02 maximum, scattered at the domain corners/boundaries rather than the interior. The Fourier spectrum tracks the reference bar-for-bar across all k=0..20 with no visible roll-off. Inference: for this smooth, spectrally-decaying problem the classical front-end is fully adequate and the network essentially exactly reproduces the solution.
cfe_q3: Same Burgers shock, but this control is even more heavily damped: the model peak only reaches ~0.55-0.60 at t=0.25 versus reference 1.0, with a broad smooth S rather than any jump. Error is a bright ~0.9 band along x=0 spreading with t. Spectrum matches only k=1 (~70) then decays hard, the model sitting at ~0.1 across k>=8 far below the reference ~1-3 plateau. Inference: this configuration is the weakest at recovering shock harmonics, behaving like a stronger low-pass than cfe_burgers.
cfe_q5: Burgers shock treated as a smooth ramp again; peak amplitude ~0.68 versus reference 1.0, with the model missing both the +1 crest and -1 trough. Error concentrates as a ~1.0 lobe on the x=0 shock line, dark elsewhere. Spectrum follows the reference to roughly k=6-7 then rolls off, model dropping to ~0.02 by k=20 against a ~1 reference floor. Inference: mid-range shock capture, comparable to cfe_burgers and clearly better than cfe_q3 but still fundamentally smoothing.
cfe_q6: Burgers shock rendered smooth, peak ~0.65 versus reference 1.0. |error| is the familiar bright ~0.9 band along x=0 fanning out with time. Spectrum matches k=1 then decays, high harmonics settling near ~0.05 for k>=12 versus the reference ~1 plateau. Inference: another low-pass control with damped shock amplitude, statistically indistinguishable from the other cfe Burgers runs and far from the reference's flat spectral tail.
conv_qapinn_base: Entangled QAPINN, 8000 iters, Burgers: despite 4x the baseline training the shock is NOT sharpened - the prediction stays a smooth ramp with peak only ~0.65 (t=0.25) versus reference 1.0, and error remains a bright ~0.9 lobe on the x=0 line. Spectrum still rolls off, high-k model coefficients ~0.04 versus reference ~1. Entanglement entropy is genuinely nonzero (von Neumann ~0.5-1.1, brightest for x<-0.5, minimum ~0.5 near x~0.25) and the per-qubit <Z> maps show real spatial structure (qubit 0 x-banded, qubits 1-3 distinct patterns). Inference: entanglement is physically present yet the long run buys no shock sharpening - the entangled ansatz stays spectrally band-limited.
conv_qapinn_entnone: No-entanglement QAPINN, 8000 iters: strikingly the shock is now crisp - the prediction shows a near-vertical transition at x=0 with peak ~0.72, and the residual is a razor-thin bright line (localized max ~1.4) exactly on x=0 with almost everything else dark. The Fourier spectrum matches the reference bar-for-bar across the full k=1..20 range (high-k model ~2 vs base's ~0.04). Entanglement entropy is numerically zero (~1e-7 scale noise), confirming no entanglement. Inference: removing entanglement dramatically improves shock capture and high-frequency content, so here the entangling layers are hurting rather than helping.
conv_cls_121: Classical net, 8000 iters, Burgers: a fairly sharp shock is recovered - the prediction has a steep transition at x=0 with peak ~0.78, but it carries visible Gibbs-like ringing (wiggles near x=0.25 at t=0.25 and faint diagonal fringes in the upper-left). Error is a bright ~1.3 streak along x=0 plus faint ringing lobes. Spectrum matches the reference across all k=1..20, model coefficients ~1-3 at high k, only slightly under. Inference: the long classical run sharpens the shock far better than the entangled QAPINN and comparably to the no-entanglement QAPINN, at the cost of some oscillatory overshoot.
seed1_ent_none: Model smears the sawtooth shock at x=0 into a smooth ramp and caps amplitude at ~0.6 (ref +/-1); spectrum matches ref for k=1-3 then rolls off monotonically below reference from k>=4. Entanglement map is flat at ~1e-7 (effectively zero), as expected for no entangler. Consistent with the ~0.45 rel-L2 pattern.
seed1_ent_linear: Shock smeared, amplitude capped ~0.6, spectrum tracks ref to k~3 then decays; entanglement entropy is now nonzero, peaking ~1.1 in the upper-x region. Consistent with the pattern.
seed1_ent_ring: Same smeared shock and ~0.6 cap, same spectral rolloff; entanglement is the largest of the seed1 variants, peaking ~1.3 near x~0.2. Otherwise consistent with the pattern.
seed1_ent_all_to_all: Shock smeared, amplitude capped ~0.65, spectral rolloff identical; entanglement peaks ~1.15 in the lower-x region. Consistent with the pattern.
seed1_cls_121: Classical control looks indistinguishable from the QAPINN variants: shock smeared, amplitude capped ~0.65, spectrum matches k=1-3 then rolls off. Consistent with the ~0.45 rel-L2 pattern.
seed2_ent_none: Smeared shock, ~0.6 amplitude cap, standard spectral rolloff beyond k~3. Consistent with the pattern.
seed2_ent_linear: Smeared shock, ~0.6 cap, spectrum tracks ref to k~3 then decays. Consistent with the pattern.
seed2_ent_ring: Visibly different spectrum: model bars stay within ~1 order of magnitude of the reference across nearly all harmonics (k up to ~20), with far less high-k rolloff than every other run; the solution itself is still shock-smeared and capped ~0.6, so this is a spectral, not accuracy, deviation.
seed2_ent_all_to_all: Smeared shock, ~0.6 cap, normal spectral rolloff. Consistent with the pattern.
seed2_cls_121: Classical control matches the QAPINN variants: smeared shock, ~0.65 cap, standard rolloff. Consistent with the pattern.
seed3_ent_none: Smeared shock, ~0.6 amplitude cap, standard spectral rolloff beyond k~3. Consistent with the pattern.
seed3_ent_linear: Smeared shock, ~0.6 cap, spectrum tracks ref to k~3 then decays. Consistent with the pattern.
seed3_ent_ring: Smeared shock, ~0.6 cap, normal spectral rolloff (no seed2-style spectral extension here). Consistent with the pattern.
seed3_ent_all_to_all: Smeared shock, ~0.6 cap, standard rolloff. Consistent with the pattern.
seed3_cls_121: Classical control indistinguishable from the QAPINN variants: smeared shock, ~0.65 cap, standard rolloff. Consistent with the pattern. nu_cls_01: nu=0.1, the SMOOTHEST point (solution bandwidth ~3). With the figure now drawn against the correct per-nu reference, the model overlays the reference almost exactly (rel-L2 0.018); the reference itself is a gently steepening sinusoid with no sharp shock, and |error| never exceeds ~0.03. Inference: at low bandwidth the depth-3 model has ample band, so the fit is near-exact -- the easy end of the continuum.
nu_cls_005: nu=0.05: the reference front is steeper than nu=0.1 but still resolved; rel-L2 rises to 0.032 as the solution's bandwidth grows. Inference: halving the viscosity roughly doubles the error -- the band is starting to bind.
nu_cls_002: nu=0.02: a distinctly sharper front; the model begins to round it and rel-L2 climbs to 0.069. Inference: the solution now demands harmonics near the edge of what a moderate net holds.
nu_cls_001: nu=0.01, the SHARPEST classical point (rel-L2 0.140). The reference has a near-discontinuous shock; the model rounds it and the residual is a bright line on x=0. Inference: this is the hard end of the continuum -- lowest viscosity, highest bandwidth, largest error, exactly as the bandwidth thesis predicts.
nu_qapinn_01: nu=0.1, depth-3 QAPINN: smooth reference well captured (rel-L2 0.049), though slightly worse than the matched classical control at the same nu (0.018). Inference: at low bandwidth the quantum layer offers no advantage -- both models have more than enough band.
nu_qapinn_005: nu=0.05, QAPINN: rel-L2 0.077, tracking the classical control (0.032) at a modest gap as the front sharpens. Inference: still no quantum advantage on the smooth-to-moderate part of the sweep.
nu_qapinn_002: nu=0.02, QAPINN: the sharpest completed QAPINN point (rel-L2 0.165), slightly worse than its matched classical (0.069). Inference: the fixed depth-3 band is out-run by the growing solution bandwidth, and the quantum layer does not rescue it -- consistent with advantage appearing only at HIGHER band (depth 5 / 6 qubits), not here.
